    What GPA do you need for the University of Hawaii?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    UH Mānoa
    generally requires a competitive GPA, with admitted students often having a 3.49–4.04 weighted range, although a 3.0 unweighted average is common. University of Hawaii at Hilo typically requires a 2.7 cumulative high school GPA. Both schools, along with University of Hawai'i–West O'ahu, may consider lower GPAs with additional test scores. 
    Key GPA Requirements by Campus 
    • UH Mānoa (Flagship): Mid-range weighted GPA is 3.49–4.04 (25th–75th percentile). It is test-optional, but holistic reviews may consider a 3.0 average unweighted GPA.
    • University of Hawaii at Hilo: Minimum 2.7 cumulative high school GPA required. A lower GPA may be considered alongside SAT/ACT scores.
    • University of Hawai'i–West O'ahu: Minimum 2.7 cumulative high school GPA required. 
    Important Considerations 
    • Holistic Review: Schools often look beyond just the GPA, evaluating curriculum rigor (AP/IB), extracurricular activities, and, in some cases, test scores.
    • Specialized Programs: Certain programs, such as Nursing or Social Work, may have higher GPA thresholds.
    • Alternative Admission: If you do not meet the minimum GPA, you may still be considered based on a holistic review of your application. 
    Note: For the most accurate and up-to-date requirements, it is recommended to visit the official University of Hawaii website.
